prerequisites: Completion of the study entry and orientation phase

learning_outcomes.text: Students are familiar with the different variants of machine tools and their areas of application.
Students are able to create simple NC programs and execute them on a machine tool.
Students know the theoretical foundations of the finite element method and have the competence to apply numerical solution methods for problems in mechatronics.
Students are able to reliably assess the application possibilities and limitations of these methods for practical use.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the operation and programming of machine tools (WZM)
Creation and processing of simple NC programs for multi-axis WZM
Expansion of knowledge about complex WZM (machining centers) with practical demonstrations and, where possible, exercises in the production area of an industrial company

Introduction to the displacement formulation of the finite element method for solving problems in linear elasticity theory (planar and spatial finite elements as well as finite elements for rods, plates, and shells)
Demonstration of the solution of practical problems in linear elasticity theory with a finite element program (linear disk, plate, and shell calculations)
Guidance for students to independently solve such problems
